diag-f1.title: Tasks in a line
diag-f1.statement: Tasks stand in a line. Task i pays pay[i]. If you take it, you must skip the next skip[i] tasks. You may also skip a task for free. What is the most you can be paid?
diag-f1.constraints: n = 4. pay and skip are given in the tiny input.
diag-f1.midLabel: most you can be paid from task 2 onward

post-f1.title: Shifts
post-f1.statement: Shifts stand in a line. Shift i pays pay[i], then you are unavailable for the next skip[i] shifts. You may pass a shift. What is the most you can earn?

diag-f2.title: Two dice
diag-f2.statement: You roll n dice, each with faces 1 through f. How many outcomes sum to target? Order counts: 1 then 3 is different from 3 then 1.
diag-f2.constraints: n, f, and target are small.
diag-f2.midLabel: outcomes for one die showing a total of 2

post-f2.title: Two dice, more faces
post-f2.statement: You roll n dice, each with faces 1 through f. How many outcomes sum to target? Order counts.
post-f2.constraints: n, f, and target are small.

diag-f3.title: Two ribbons
diag-f3.statement: You have two ribbons. You may delete a letter from either. What is the fewest deletions so the ribbons become equal?
diag-f3.midLabel: length of the longest common subsequence

post-f3.title: Two names
post-f3.statement: Two names. Delete the fewest letters, from either name, so the remaining letters match in order.

diag-f4a.title: At least double
diag-f4a.statement: A row of numbers. Take a subsequence where each chosen value is at least twice the one chosen before it. How long is the longest such subsequence?
diag-f4a.constraints: The row is short. Order in the row must be kept.
diag-f4a.midLabel: length of the longest subsequence ending at 2

post-f4a.title: Doubling picks
post-f4a.statement: Pick a subsequence. Each picked value must be at least twice the previously picked value. How long is the longest pick?
post-f4a.constraints: Order in the row is fixed.

diag-f4b.title: Three balloons
diag-f4b.statement: Balloons in a row hold the values given. Bursting a balloon scores the product of its two current neighbors. Balloons already burst are gone. Pad both ends with a permanent 1 that you never burst. What is the most you can score?
diag-f4b.midLabel: score of bursting the middle balloon last, with neighbors 3 and 5 still there

post-f4b.title: Four balloons
post-f4b.statement: Same balloon rules. Permanent 1s at both ends. Burst every balloon inside, scoring neighbor products. What is the most you can score?
post-f4b.midLabel: score if 5 is burst last among the open range whose ends are the permanent 1s, which is not a legal single step on the whole row

diag-f5.title: A pass that rests
diag-f5.statement: Prices, one per day. You may buy, sell, or rest. After you sell, you must rest for one day before you buy again. You hold at most one share. What is the most profit?
diag-f5.midLabel: profit of resting through the first day and then buying the second

post-f5.title: Another pass
post-f5.statement: Same rules: at most one share, and a sale forces a rest day before the next buy. Most profit?
post-f5.midLabel: profit if you only buy on day 0 and sell on day 1

diag-f6.title: Chore sessions
diag-f6.statement: Chores have durations. A session holds at most limit minutes. A chore cannot be split. What is the fewest sessions that finish every chore?
diag-f6.midLabel: fewest sessions for only the first chore

post-f6.title: Errands
post-f6.statement: Errands have durations. A block of time holds at most limit. No errand is split. Fewest blocks?
post-f6.midLabel: blocks for the single errand of length 3

card-746.title: Paid steps
card-746.statement: Steps cost cost[i] to leave. You may start on step 0 or step 1, and from step i you go to i + 1 or i + 2. Reach the top, which is past the last step. What is the cheapest way?
card-746.midLabel: cheapest cost to stand at the second step, before paying to leave it

card-746b.title: Toll booths
card-746b.statement: Booths charge toll[i] when you leave them. From a booth you walk one or two booths ahead. You may start at the first or the second. Reach past the last booth as cheaply as you can.
card-746b.midLabel: cheapest cost to reach the top from having arrived at booth 0 for free

card-55.title: A hallway of hops
card-55.statement: You stand on index 0. From index i you may hop at most nums[i] steps forward. Can you reach the last index?
card-55.constraints: The hallway is short. This may not want a table.
card-55.answerLabel: can you reach the last index (yes or no)

card-139.title: A glued sentence
card-139.statement: A string and a dictionary. Can the string be cut into dictionary words, with no letters left over?
card-139.constraints: The string is short. Words may repeat.
card-139.answerLabel: can it be cut (yes or no)

card-139b.title: Tiles
card-139b.statement: Tiles spell a row. You have a box of words. Can the row be tiled by those words, using a word more than once?
card-139b.tiny: s = catsandog, words = cats, dog, sand, and, cat
card-139b.answerLabel: can it be tiled (yes or no)

card-213.title: A circular street
card-213.statement: Houses in a circle hold money. You cannot rob two adjacent houses, and the first and last are adjacent. What is the most you can rob?
card-213.constraints: The street is short. One house is allowed.
card-213.midLabel: most on the line that drops the last house

card-213b.title: A round of lamps
card-213b.statement: Lamps in a circle. Taking a lamp yields its value and forbids the two neighbors. The first and the last are neighbors. Most value?
card-213b.midLabel: most on the line that drops the first lamp

card-f1-stalls.title: Stalls
card-f1-stalls.statement: Stalls in a straight line, not a circle. Taking stall i earns value[i] and forbids the next stall. Most you can earn?
card-f1-stalls.midLabel: most from the first three stalls

card-f1-hops.title: Hops
card-f1-hops.statement: A frog hops 1 or 2 pads. How many ways to reach pad n? Order of hops matters. The frog starts off the board, before pad 1, and pad n is the goal.

card-53.title: A run of numbers
card-53.statement: A row of numbers, negatives allowed. A non-empty contiguous run. What is the largest sum of any run?
card-53.constraints: The row is the classic short one.
card-53.midLabel: largest run that ends at the 4 which follows -3

card-2140-alt.title: Exams
card-2140-alt.statement: Questions in order. Solving question i scores points[i] and then you must skip the next brain[i] questions. You may skip any question. Most points?
card-2140-alt.constraints: Four questions. This is the alternate if you already know the famous writeup.

card-coins-6.title: Stamps
card-coins-6.statement: Stamp values may be reused. You need to make an amount. What is the fewest stamps? If you cannot, the answer is -1.
card-coins-6.constraints: Values 1, 3, and 4. Amount 6. Greedy is a trap.

card-squares.title: Square tiles
card-squares.statement: Tiles whose sides are perfect squares: 1, 4, 9, and so on. You may reuse a size. Fewest tiles to fill an area of n?

card-subset-11.title: A split of coins
card-subset-11.statement: Coins with positive values. Can some of them, each used at most once, sum to target?
card-subset-11.answerLabel: can you make the target (yes or no)

card-subset-b.title: Packing books
card-subset-b.statement: Books have weights. Can a subset of them weigh exactly target, each book at most once?

card-518.title: Unordered change
card-518.statement: Coins may be reused. How many combinations make amount? Order does not count: 1 + 2 is the same combination as 2 + 1.

card-518b.title: Soup scoops
card-518b.statement: Scoops of sizes in the list, unlimited. How many combinations fill a bowl of the given size? The order of scoops does not make a new combination.
card-518b.constraints: sizes 1 and 2, bowl 4. This is the alternate if you already know the coin writeup.

card-377.title: Ordered change
card-377.statement: Numbers may be reused. How many ordered sequences sum to the target? 1 then 2 is different from 2 then 1.

card-377b.title: Playlists
card-377b.statement: Songs have lengths. A playlist is an ordered list of songs, and a song may repeat. How many playlists last exactly the target minutes?

card-474.title: Zeros and ones
card-474.statement: Strings of 0s and 1s. You may take a subset. You have at most m zeros and n ones in total. What is the most strings you can take?
card-474.constraints: m = 5 zeros, n = 3 ones. Five strings.
card-474.midLabel: most strings with at most 1 zero and 1 one

card-474b.title: Red and blue beads
card-474b.statement: Necklaces cost red beads and blue beads. You have at most R red and B blue. Each necklace at most once. Most necklaces?
card-474b.midLabel: most necklaces with no blue beads and one red

card-494.title: Plus and minus
card-494.statement: Numbers, each used once, each given a plus or a minus. How many ways make the expression equal target?
card-494.constraints: The row is short. Zeros matter.
card-494.midLabel: ways to make a positive part of 1, before the algebra

card-494b.title: Two pans
card-494b.statement: Weights, each placed on the left pan or the right pan. How many ways does the right pan exceed the left by exactly the difference?
card-494b.constraints: Five weights of 1. Difference 3. Same arithmetic as plus and minus.
card-494b.midLabel: subsets of the weights that sum to 2

card-f2-cold-01.title: A locker
card-f2-cold-01.statement: Codes are positive integers, each used at most once. Can they sum to exactly the target?
card-f2-cold-01.constraints: This is the cold problem for the day you meet 0/1.

decoy-gas.title: A loop of fuel
decoy-gas.statement: Stations in a circle. station i has gas[i] and costs cost[i] to reach the next station. You may start at one station. Can you complete one loop, and if so where do you start? If several, any legal start is fine. If none, answer -1.
decoy-gas.constraints: This looks like a circular table. It may not be one.

decoy-stock1.title: One purchase
decoy-stock1.statement: Prices, one per day. You may buy once and sell once later. You may also do nothing. What is the most profit?
decoy-stock1.constraints: This looks like a day-by-day mode. A running minimum may be enough.
decoy-stock1.midLabel: lowest price seen before the last day

card-paths.title: A small grid
card-paths.statement: A grid with m rows and n columns. From a cell you may step down or right. How many ways from the top-left corner to the bottom-right?
card-paths.midLabel: ways to reach the cell in row 2, column 1, counting from 1

card-obstacles.title: Blocked cells
card-obstacles.statement: Same down-or-right walks. Some cells are blocked and contribute 0. How many walks from the top-left to the bottom-right?
card-obstacles.constraints: A 2 by 2 grid with one block.

card-health.title: A short cave
card-health.statement: A grid of signed numbers. Entering a cell adds its number to your health. Health must stay at least 1 after every cell, including the last. You step only right or down. What is the least health you need when you enter the top-left, so that some path survives?
card-health.midLabel: least health when entering the bottom-right cell

card-lcs-short.title: Shared letters
card-lcs-short.statement: Two words. A common subsequence need not be contiguous. How long is the longest one?
card-lcs-short.midLabel: LCS of the prefix ab and the prefix a

card-edit-short.title: One word into another
card-edit-short.statement: Turn word a into word b. A step inserts, deletes, or replaces one letter. How few steps?
card-edit-short.midLabel: steps to turn h into nothing

card-115-ways.title: Hidden word
card-115-ways.statement: How many times does word t appear as a subsequence of word s? The letters of t must stay in order. They need not be contiguous.
card-115-ways.midLabel: ways for t's first letter inside s's first letter

card-lis-short.title: Increasing picks
card-lis-short.statement: A row. Pick a strictly increasing subsequence, not necessarily contiguous. How long is the longest?
card-lis-short.constraints: The short row from the lesson's cousin.
card-lis-short.midLabel: length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at 7

card-count-lis.title: How many longest
card-count-lis.statement: How many distinct longest strictly increasing subsequences does the row contain? Two subsequences are different when their index lists differ.

card-pal-count.title: Palindromic slices
card-pal-count.statement: How many slices of the string are palindromes? Single letters count. Different positions count even when the letters match.
card-pal-count.midLabel: is the whole string a palindrome (yes or no)

card-lps.title: A palindrome inside
card-lps.statement: A subsequence that reads the same forward and backward. How long is the longest one inside the string?
card-lps.midLabel: length inside the single letter s[0]

card-stick.title: Cutting a rod
card-stick.statement: A rod of length n. You must make the cuts in the list, in any order. A cut costs the length of the current piece you cut. What is the cheapest order?
card-stick.constraints: n = 7, cuts at 1, 3, and 4. Add the ends 0 and n.
card-stick.midLabel: cost of a piece with no cut left inside it

card-fee.title: A toll on the sale
card-fee.statement: Prices, one per day. You may buy and sell as often as you like, holding at most one share. Each sale pays the price minus a fee. What is the most profit?
card-fee.constraints: fee = 2. This is not the cooldown problem.
card-fee.midLabel: profit of buying at 1 and selling at 3, after the fee

card-two-tx.title: At most two sales
card-two-tx.statement: Prices, one per day. At most two sales, meaning at most two buys. Hold at most one share. Most profit?
card-two-tx.constraints: The row is long enough for two trades.
card-two-tx.midLabel: most profit with at most one sale

card-mode-original.title: A job with a rest day
card-mode-original.statement: Each day you may work the job, which pays pay[i], or rest. Working forbids working the next day. You may rest as often as you like. Most pay? This is a cold problem, and it is not a stock fee.
card-mode-original.midLabel: most pay from the first day alone

card-tree-rob.title: A small tree of houses
card-tree-rob.statement: Houses form a tree. The root holds 3. Its left child holds 2 and has one child holding 3. Its right child holds 3 and has one child holding 1. You cannot rob a house and its child. What is the most you can rob?
card-tree-rob.tiny: root 3; left 2 with child 3; right 3 with child 1
card-tree-rob.midLabel: most from the left subtree if you do not rob the left child

card-1799-alt.title: Pair scores
card-1799-alt.statement: nums has 2n numbers, here n = 1 so two numbers. Operation i, starting at 1, removes two remaining numbers and scores i * gcd of them. With two numbers there is one operation. What is the score?
card-1799-alt.constraints: Two numbers. The famous longer version is the same state on a bigger set.

card-279.title: Square stamps
card-279.statement: Postage n must be made of square stamp values 1, 4, 9, ... You may reuse a value. Fewest stamps?

card-1049.title: Two piles of stones
card-1049.statement: Stones with positive weights. Split them into two piles. The score is the absolute difference of the pile weights. What is the smallest score?
card-1049.midLabel: whether a subset sums to 11, half of 23 rounded down is 11, yes or no

card-718.title: A shared run
card-718.statement: Two rows of numbers. A common subarray is contiguous in both. How long is the longest one?
card-718.constraints: This is not a subsequence. A mismatch resets.
card-718.midLabel: length of the common run that ends at a[2] and b[0], both 3

card-152.title: A product run
card-152.statement: A row of numbers, negatives allowed. A non-empty contiguous run. What is the largest product of any run?
card-152.constraints: Negatives flip the best and the worst.
card-152.midLabel: largest product of a run ending at -2

card-1262.title: Divisible by three
card-1262.statement: A row of numbers. Delete as few as you like, possibly none. The remaining sum should be divisible by 3, and as large as possible. The empty remaining sum is 0.
card-1262.constraints: The extra dimension is the sum modulo 3.
card-1262.midLabel: largest sum with remainder 1, or none

card-mod-b.title: Threes
card-mod-b.statement: Same rule: delete any subset, maximize the remaining sum, and the sum must be divisible by 3.

card-1289.title: A falling path with a twist
card-1289.statement: A grid of non-negative numbers. You start anywhere in the top row and fall to the bottom. From a cell you may step to any cell in the next row except the same column. What is the cheapest path?
card-1289.constraints: A 3 by 3 grid. This is not ordinary falling-path, which allows the same column.
card-1289.midLabel: cheapest way to reach row 1, column 0

card-fall-ordinary.title: Ordinary falling
card-fall-ordinary.statement: Fall from any cell on the top row to the bottom. A step goes to the next row, to the same column or a neighbor column. Cheapest path?
card-fall-ordinary.midLabel: cheapest way to reach row 1, column 1

card-97.title: Two strings woven
card-97.statement: Can s3 be formed by interleaving s1 and s2, keeping the order of each? Use every letter.
card-97.tiny: s1 = aabcc, s2 = dbbca, s3 = aadbbcbcac
card-97.midLabel: does the empty prefix of both match the empty prefix of s3 (yes or no)

card-interleave-b.title: Two queues
card-interleave-b.statement: Two queues and a target line. You may take the front of either queue. Can you build the line, using every person?
card-interleave-b.tiny: s1 = ab, s2 = cd, s3 = acbd
card-interleave-b.answerLabel: can you build it (yes or no)
card-interleave-b.midLabel: can the first letter of s3 come from s1

card-1039.title: A polygon
card-1039.statement: A convex polygon has vertex values. A triangle of vertices i, j, k scores values[i] * values[j] * values[k]. Triangulate the polygon. What is the minimum total score? For a triangle, the score is the single product.

card-burst-alt.title: Three tokens
card-burst-alt.statement: Tokens in a row, permanent 1s at the ends. Removing a token scores the product of its current neighbors. Remove all of them. Most score?
card-burst-alt.constraints: Three tokens. Alternate if you already know the balloon writeup.
card-burst-alt.midLabel: score of removing the middle token last while 2 and 4 are its neighbors

card-sessions-b.title: Two chores
card-sessions-b.statement: Two chores, durations 3 and 3. A session holds 3. Fewest sessions?
card-sessions-b.midLabel: sessions for a single chore of length 3

card-tree-line.title: A tree that is a line
card-tree-line.statement: Three houses in a line, which is a tree: 4, then 1, then 4. You cannot rob neighbors. Most?
card-tree-line.midLabel: most if the middle house is robbed

card-931.title: Falling path
card-931.statement: A grid. Start at any cell of the top row. A step moves to the next row, same column or either neighbor. What is the minimum sum to the bottom row?
card-931.midLabel: minimum sum to reach row 1, column 2

aloud-1.title: Said aloud
aloud-1.statement: Jobs in a line. Job i pays pay[i] and then blocks the next block[i] jobs. You may skip a job. Most pay? Say the sentence out loud before you write it. You have 12 minutes for the sentence.
aloud-1.constraints: Four jobs. This card is only for the mock after the posttest.

card-rest-b.title: Rest between jobs
card-rest-b.statement: Jobs pay the given amounts. Working a job forbids working the next day. Most pay?
card-rest-b.constraints: Three days. A variant of the rest-day job.
card-rest-b.midLabel: pay of the first job alone
